name: Habsburg Partition of Austria, Dynastic Division
summary: The Treaty of Neuberg (1379) divides Habsburg Austria between Duke Albert III (Austria proper) and Duke Leopold III (Styria, Carinthia, Tyrol, Further Austria). This 'Albertine-Leopoldine' division lasts until Albert V reunifies the dynasty (1424). The repeated Habsburg partitions reflect the Carolingian inheritance law that treated territories as family property rather than indivisible states.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Austrian partition demonstrates why the Habsburg imperial project required abolishing the partition inheritance system; Emperor Frederick III's use of the motto AEIOU (Alles Erdreich ist Österreich untertan, All the world is subject to Austria) reflects Habsburg aspirations that partition constantly undermines; Maximilian I's concentration of the inheritance was essential to the Charles V empire
